title: Relative clauses with a preposition: the articles of the Constitution

sections.content: You know relative clauses with *que* from B1 Unit 5 and, with a preposition, *el que*, *la que*, *los que* and *las que* from B1 Unit 20 (*un servicio del que dependen muchas personas*). Put the preposition before the article and match it to the noun. Use them to describe the Constitution of 1917 and the people it was written for.

items.spanish: El artículo 27 es el artículo en el que se habla de la tierra.
items.english: Article 27 is the article in which the land is discussed.

items.spanish: La Constitución de 1857 era la ley con la que se gobernaba el país.
items.english: The Constitution of 1857 was the law with which the country was governed.

items.spanish: Los obreros son las personas para las que se escribió el artículo 123.
items.english: The workers are the people for whom Article 123 was written.

items.spanish: Querétaro es la ciudad en la que se reunieron los diputados.
items.english: Querétaro is the city in which the deputies met.

sections.content: The article agrees with the noun before it (*el artículo en el que*, *la ley con la que*, *los derechos de los que*), and the preposition stays with the verb that needs it. Never leave the preposition out: not *el artículo que se habla de la tierra*.
